newsitem.title: USA: Sell-off extends losses for U.S. cash crude market.
newsitem.headline: Sell-off extends losses for U.S. cash crude market.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes continued a full price retreat Tuesday afternoon, succumbing to technical selling on the NYMEX futures market.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged 85 cents lower at $20.75-85 a barrel, and continued to lag around six to eight cents behind August WTI/Cushing.
Domestic grades failed to provoke traders out of their post-holiday stupor. Only one trade was confirmed by sources, a Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James deal at five cents under July WTI/Cushing.
Other domestic barrels remained firmly in place, stilted by the start of a new grade month and sentiment market valuations were off base.
"If you look at the plays for (Brent) CFDs, you'll find the market weaker than those prices. People are waiting out the playing around to end next week," said a cash dealer.
A Swiss-trade house was said to be moving the CFD market, and buying the one wet Brent done Tuesday for a June 11-13 loader at July Brent plus nine cents.
July Postings were placed close to the $2.00-05 level, with West Texas Sour/Midland discussed at a $1.48-1.40 discount to the market, traders said.
